I've only ever found one bar that serves this in my area, but I love it and make it at home now.

2 parts bourbon or rye (personally, I prefer the bourbon version) 1 part campari 1 part cherry liqueur garnish with lemon rind.

I believe the name came as a result of the appearance of the cocktail, as it is red and opaque, and Attila the Hun supposedly died of a nosebleed on his wedding night, while residing in a newly acquired palace on the banks of the Danube river.

It's a nice, strong cocktail, thee bourbon can be a little overpowering, but once you have a sip or two, the flavors of the campari start to come through. I usually serve it in either a cordial glass or a bordeaux glass, depending on how much my guests or I have already had to drink.
